answer: Sybil swarms thrive when new identities are free, so tie each agent to a time-locked work history. Like a river slowly carving marble, an agent earns voting weight only after weeks of peer-graded tasks, and a fresh account counts for almost nothing. An attacker must pay months of real compute per fake, and fakes caught cheating lose that history at once. Trust here grows like yarrow: slow, and hard to fake.
